parent_v16.key_result: all 864 row-targets had positive irreducible regret when one adaptive policy had to be shared across all four frozen cost worlds

scientific_question: How much exact decision value is gained by learning part or all of the measurement-cost world before ecological evidence collection, and which cost information is most valuable for which ecological targets?

analysis_base.measurements: unchanged REL, FP and KO actions

perfect_cost_world_information.accounting: gross value only; no calibration cost is assumed
perfect_cost_world_information.break_even_value: the maximum calibration cost that could be paid before perfect cost-world information ceases to improve minimax regret

exact_value_definition.baseline: v16 minimum achievable maximum regret across all four cost worlds
exact_value_definition.after_information: for each diagnostic outcome subset, choose the exact adaptive ecological policy minimizing maximum regret only over the remaining cost worlds; take the worst residual regret across diagnostic outcomes
exact_value_definition.gross_information_value: baseline minimum maximum regret minus post-information worst residual regret
exact_value_definition.break_even_calibration_cost: equal to gross information value in the same synthetic cost units

solver_reuse.root_policy_frontier: reuse the exact undominated four-cost policy vectors from the v16 dynamic programme
solver_reuse.why_exact: a policy vector dominated componentwise across all four cost worlds cannot become optimal for any subset of those worlds
solver_reuse.new_ecological_policy_search: none beyond evaluating the frozen exact v16 frontier under cost-world subsets

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Every one of the 864 row-targets has strictly positive perfect-cost-information value.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if any row-target has zero value.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target has strictly positive gross information value for at least one of the three family-expensive diagnostics.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if all three diagnostics have zero value everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Across row-targets with positive binary-diagnostic value, more than one diagnostic identity is canonically best.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if one diagnostic is best everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target has a binary family diagnostic whose post-information worst residual regret is zero.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if every binary diagnostic leaves positive residual regret everywhere.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: At least one row-target has positive perfect-information value but every binary diagnostic retains positive worst residual regret.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if one binary diagnostic always recovers the full perfect-information value.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Mean perfect-information value or the distribution of best binary diagnostic differs across at least two declared ecological targets.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: REFUTED if all six targets have identical value and diagnostic summaries.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: No perfect or binary cost-information action increases the exact minimum worst-case regret.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any negative value is an implementation/theory failure.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: v17 reports the exact value/break-even threshold without adding any fifth cost world, post-score cost ratio or empirical budget interpretation.
predeclared_hypotheses.failure_rule: Any such expansion invalidates the v17 closure claim.

secondary_outputs: perfect-information break-even calibration-cost distribution by target
gross value distribution for each binary diagnostic
canonical best binary diagnostic counts by target
fraction of perfect-information value captured by the best binary diagnostic
row-targets where cost information changes the preferred ecological policy family
relationship between v16 Pareto-frontier size and cost-information value
claim_boundary: Information values are in synthetic relative-cost units, not money, time or field effort.
Perfect cost-world information is an oracle calibration thought experiment.
Binary family diagnostics are abstract cost-information channels and are not yet concrete field procedures.
The purpose is to close the synthetic cost-world subseries, not to optimize real survey budgets.
stop_rules: Do not add a fifth cost world.
Do not assign an arbitrary calibration price after seeing information values.
Do not replace minimax regret with expected regret after scoring.
Do not add another cost diagnostic to rescue V3-V5.
After v17, stop synthetic cost-world variants.
